title: The Frohmanian Tether on SDiff(T^3): A Metriplectic Correction, Its Canonicity, and an Obstruction to Damping
notes: Copyright (c) 2026 Benjamin Stanley Frohman. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. This record is NOT a proof of global regularity of the 3D Navier-Stokes equations and makes no claim toward the Clay Millennium Problem.
description: Lean 4 (v4.30.0-rc1) / Mathlib (v4.30.0-rc1) formalization and manuscript on the Frohmanian tether T(F,G) = -kappa ||omega||^2 int <Pi_u dF, Pi_u dG>, a symmetric quadratic correction to the Arnold Lie-Poisson bracket. Proved: symmetry and negative feedback (C3) unconditionally; kinetic-energy degeneracy (C2) conditional on the named hypothesis KineticEnergyDerivIsVelocity (believed false as stated), div u = 0 and finite energy; coadjoint invariance (C1) conditional on SDiffActionHyp and TetherIntegralPreserved; canonicity only from diagonal saturation and polarization; and an obstruction to damping: every symmetric kernel satisfying (C2) has B(H,M) = 0 for every functional M, so the tether's damping coefficient is 0. The analytic layer proves a comparison lemma for y' <= C y^2 - k y^3 and conditional implications in which the cubic rate or closing bound, Kato local existence, Beale-Kato-Majda continuation and uniqueness are explicit open hypotheses. Build: 2712 jobs; 519 theorem constants (483 stated in the sources, 36 auto-generated) and 761 declarations audited; no sorry, no native_decide, no axiom declarations; only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (enforced in CI). Not a proof of Navier-Stokes global regularity; no Clay claim.
